newsitem.title: ITALY: Show cancelled as Versace murder numbs Italians.
newsitem.headline: Show cancelled as Versace murder numbs Italians.

text.p: A glamorous fashion gala to end Rome's week of catwalk shows was cancelled on Tuesday as fellow designers, friends and celebrities he clothed voiced shock and horror at the murder in Miami Beach of Gianni Versace.
Bewildered and teary-eyed models stopped their fittings as organisers decided to indefinitely postpone Wednesday's gala finale to Rome's "alta moda" (haute couture) week on the elegant Spanish Steps.

"Gianni was a friend," said film director Franco Zeffirelli, "Italy and the world have lost a stylist but I have lost a dear person. I knew of the slight melancholy that existed beneath his image of vitality, of energy.
"There was a sword of Damacles hanging over his soul. The tragic manner of his death seems almost like an atrocious fulfillment of his destiny."
"There are no words to describe how I feel right now," said top designer Gianfranco Ferre. "What happened is absurd, unexplainable, terrible...I feel only infinite pain."
Versace, a smiling silver-haired figure seen at the shows in Milan, London, Paris and New York, symbolised Italian fashion the world over and his killing sent shivers through the industry.
In Milan, the spiritual home of Italian high fashion, the shutters were pulled on Versace's shop as the innovative design house he founded tried to come to terms with his death.
Versace's brother Santo and sister Donatella left the city to fly to Miami on a private jet.
Designers, politicians and film directors paid homage to the man who clothed Princess Diana, Monaco's Princess Caroline, singer Elton John and other celebrities.
Princess Diana, in a statement issued from the South of France where she is on holiday, said: "I am devastated by the loss of a great and talented man."
The designer named a handbag after her -- The Lady Di. But their friendship was strained when the princess pulled out of a book venture with the designer.
"My reaction is one of revolt against such an unnatural and violent death and one of profound grief," said Giorgio Armani, another of Italy's top designers.
"Gianni was young and talented, and he worked so hard," Armani said in a statement, noting that Versace had recently overcome a serious illness. He had been suffering from cancer.
Armani praised Versace's "dignity, embracing life with energy and a tremendous desire to accomplish things".
Another of Italy's great contemporary stylists, Valentino, said: "The shock of this tragedy devastates me. I can't believe he's not still with us."
"I am shocked, incredulous, in pain over this tragic news," said designer Mariuccia Mandelli, who goes by the professional name Krizia. "I am so upset that I can't bring myself to say anything more."
"It's incredible news," said Nicola Trussardi, another top Italian fashion name. "There's absolute disbelief here and we're deeply upset.
"He was someone who had made an incredible contribution to Italian fashion. The man and the family have left their mark on the history of Italian fashion," Trussardi said.
The Fendi sisters, designers of exclusive leather goods and furs, said Versace's name would live on in his designs.
"A creativity like his can never die," Carla Fendi said in a statement. "We're sure that his name will live on after him.
Supermodel Kate Moss, currently working in Jamaica, said in a statement issued from her London agent: "I'm stunned and lost for words."
Valeria Mazza, an Argentine model who worked with Versace, said she heard about the murder while she was fitting.
"He was a great man," she said. "He is the one who discovered me."
British fashion designers paid tribute to Versace.

1960s fashion icon Mary Quant said: "He was all about life. His designs were immediately recognisable as rich, glamorous and sexy. He dared to use a strong dash of vulgarity just beautifully. He was a man who everyone adored."
Punk queen Vivienne Westwood said: "He was obviously one of the most talented and famous designers of the last few years."
Rock star Elton John, no stranger to Versace's creations, was too upset to make a public statement after hearing the news on holiday in Nice, south of France.
"He's completely shocked and numb with disbelief about the whole thing," a spokesman said.
British actress Elizabeth Hurley said in statement: "Gianni was a dear friend of mine and I am going to miss him horribly."
A black dress, slashed almost to the navel and held together with safety pins, propelled Hurley from obscurity to the front pages when she wore it to the premiere of "Four Weddings And A Funeral".
